title: On Laughing at the oldest joke again
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：laugh　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 laugh 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1985 the director ① laughed at the oldest joke again in public, and every actor in the theatre said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the director ② laughs at the oldest joke again in silence without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ laugh at the oldest joke again at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ laughed at the oldest joke again before — a line in the poster for August 1979 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Laughing at the oldest joke again in public, the director said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ laugh the matter off at supper in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Laugh the matter off at supper at once and never mention it again.

By 1992 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the poster, and a new actor from the next theatre ⑧ laughs the matter off at supper in public every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stage, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ laughed at the oldest joke again again when nobody else would.

⑩ To laugh at the oldest joke again, my mother said in 1997, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the theatre remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the theatre forgets, somebody laughs at the oldest joke again in silence again and somebody must laugh at the oldest joke again in public all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 笑（一般过去式 laughed at the oldest joke again：1985 年导演头一回这样做，当着众人面）
B. v. 笑（一般现在 laughs at the oldest joke again：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 笑（不定式 to laugh at the oldest joke again：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 笑（过去完成时 had laughed at the oldest joke again：1979 年八月的戏报上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 笑（动名词 laughing at the oldest joke again 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 笑着说（laugh the matter off at supper：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去笑着说在晚饭桌上把这事一笑了之）
G. v. 笑着说（laugh the matter off at supper：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 笑（后段两处：新来的演员照例 laughs the matter off at supper，而母亲又一次 laughed at the oldest joke again）

answers.why: laugh 意为“笑”，1985 年导演当着众人面笑又为那个老笑话笑起来，那是戏院里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 laughed。
laugh 意为“笑”，自那以后导演一言不发地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 laughs。
laugh 意为“笑”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯笑又为那个老笑话笑起来”，此处为不定式 to laugh at the oldest joke again。
laugh 意为“笑”，戏报里 八月 那行字说明早在 1992 年之前就有人笑过，故用过去完成时 had laughed。
laugh 意为“笑”，导演说“笑又为那个老笑话笑起来这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 laughing at the oldest joke again 作主语。
laugh 意为“笑着说”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去笑着说在晚饭桌上把这事一笑了之”，should ever 之后用原形 laugh the matter off at supper。
laugh 意为“笑着说”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻笑着说在晚饭桌上把这事一笑了之（laugh the matter off at supper at once），以后再也不要提起。
laugh 意为“笑”，新来的演员每个夜晚都照例笑着说在晚饭桌上把这事一笑了之，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 laughs。
laugh 意为“笑”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当着众人面笑又为那个老笑话笑起来，用一般过去式 laughed 叙述。
laugh 意为“笑”，结尾那句是母亲 1997 年的话：要笑又为那个老笑话笑起来，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和戏院记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 laugh 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1985 the director laughed at the oldest joke again in public, and nobody in the theatre forgot it.
Even now the director laughs at the oldest joke again in silence whenever the theatre asks.
Laughing at the oldest joke again in public, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever laugh the matter off at supper in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new actor from the next theatre laughs the matter off at supper in public every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother laughed at the oldest joke again again, and the theatre remembered that half.
